title: Correctness of the search circuit
statement: Let $n,m$ be natural numbers, let $R$ be a relation between Boolean lists, and let $(D_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ be a family of Boolean circuits, with $D_j$ taking $n+j$ input bits. Suppose every $D_j$ is well formed, has fan-in at most two, and, for each $1\le j\le m$, every Boolean list $y$ of length $n$ and list $p$ of length $j$ satisfy: $D_j$ outputs true on their concatenation exactly when $p$ has an extension of length $m$ related to $y$ by $R$. For any input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, if there is a length-$m$ list related to the list of bits of $x$ by $R$, then the search circuit built from this family outputs a list of length $m$ that is related to the list of bits of $x$ by $R$.
hypotheses_covered: Every circuit $D_j$ is well formed and has fan-in at most two
For every $j$ with $1\le j\le m$, the circuit test is equivalent to existence of an $R$-related length-$m$ extension
There exists a length-$m$ list $v$ with $R(\operatorname{bits}(x),v)$
